item.title: The Agentic Wild West & Sovereign AI
item.description: We analyze the alarming security gaps in the Model Context Protocol and OpenClaw marketplaces. Plus, how developers are building machine-first routing, optimizing 17MB speech engines for agents, and why nations are investing billions in sovereign AI infrastructure.

item.title: Hallucinations, Protocols, and Sovereign AI
item.description: Today on The Dev Journal: engineers and markets collide. We unpack NVIDIA’s Dynamo redesign and the inference-layer tradeoffs reshaping distributed AI, the push for standardization with the Fast Model Context Protocol, and why old-school classifiers still win in certain tasks. Then we expose a systemic failure in automated financial reporting — repeated ticker hallucinations that could mislead traders — and trace the engineering faults behind it. Along the way we cover Interop 2026 browser wins, performance wins from native CSS features, and what sovereign AI investment means for infrastructure and risk. Concise, technical, and grounded in data — Sloane and Vance break down the facts, the stakes, and what engineers should do next.

item.title: Friction Matters — Dynamo, MCP, and the Apple Conundrum
item.description: Sloane and Vance unpack how engineering teams are cutting operational tax and where that leads us. We dissect NVIDIA’s Dynamo v0.9.0 (the ZMQ Event Plane, FlashIndexer and multi‑modal disaggregation), an Obsidian→Anki pipeline for developer learning, Monk Mode’s deep‑work approach, and the rise of Model Context Protocol / FastMCP for standardized AI integrations. Plus a methodical comparison of TF‑IDF vs. LLM embeddings on the BBC dataset, and a market primer on Apple — strong fundamentals but limited near‑term catalysts and low confidence in short‑term upside. Technical, evidence‑driven, and actionable — Sloane and Vance ground opinions in concrete facts so engineers and investors know what to watch next.
